# Marks fixtures

**Origin**: `Marks.db3` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`) of a stock SAS.Planet install,
captured 2026-09-17.

**Backend confirmed**: this install uses the **SQLite (`Marks.db3`) backend**, not the legacy
`.sml` XML format — no `.sml` file exists anywhere on the live install or in the legacy repo's
`Test/` tree (searched both). So this fixture set only covers the SQLite/mORMot backend.

**How sliced**: copied the live `Marks.db3` + `Marks.db3-wal` + `Marks.db3-shm` to a scratch
location, ran `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);` there to fold the WAL into the main file (so the
fixture is a single self-contained `.db3`, no companion `-wal`/`-shm` needed), then copied the
result here. The legacy tree was never touched. `VACUUM` was attempted but fails under the stock
`sqlite3` CLI with `no such collation sequence: SYSTEMNOCASE` — the app registers a custom
`SYSTEMNOCASE` collation at runtime (via mORMot) that plain `sqlite3` doesn't have, so the file
was left un-vacuumed (124 KB, still tiny). **This is itself a finding for ADR-0005**: any C++
reader/writer for `Marks.db3` must register an ASCII case-insensitive collation named
`SYSTEMNOCASE` before opening the DB, or every text column (`uName`, `cName`, `mName`, `mDesc`,
`miName`) will fail to open/query correctly.

**Content**: this live install has never had any marks created — `Mark`, `Category`,
`MarkImage`, `MarkView`, `CategoryView`, `MarkAppearance`, `MarkMeta` are all empty (0 rows).
Only `User` has one row: `(ID=1, uName='sasgis')` — the default user created on first run.
`MarkRTree_node` has 1 row (empty R-tree root node). This means the fixture exercises **schema
and empty-state handling only**, not actual mark geometry (WKB blobs, appearance/color codec,
80-bit Extended-float codec mentioned in CHARTER risk #5) — no real mark data was available from
either source for this ticket. Flagged as an open question: a follow-up ticket should either
hand-craft a minimal `INSERT` (state as synthetic per protocol rule 10) or obtain a real populated
`Marks.db3` before the marks-DB reader is implemented/tested against actual geometry.

**`Marks.db3.schema.sql`**: full `.schema` dump (all `CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE INDEX`/
`CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` statements) taken from this fixture with `sqlite3 Marks.db3 ".schema"`.
Confirms: `Mark.mGeoWKB` is a BLOB (WKB geometry), full-text search via `MarkFTS` (fts4,
`tokenize=simple`), spatial index via `MarkRTree` (rtree module), and the `SYSTEMNOCASE`
collation used on every user-facing text column — this is the literal DDL needed for ADR-0005
since the schema is not present verbatim in the legacy Pascal source.

**What it exercises**: FEAT items for marks-DB open/schema-validation, empty-database handling,
default-user bootstrap, and (via the schema dump) the exact column/type/collation/index contract
the new C++ reader must replicate byte-for-byte.

## `SASPlanet.marks-sections.ini` (added 2026-10-12 with docs/specs/marks.md)

**Origin**: `SASPlanet.ini` (the same stock SAS.Planet install), sections
`[MarkSystemConfig]`, `[MarkNewPoint]`, `[MarkNewPoint_Name]`, `[MarkNewLine]`, `[MarkNewLine_Name]`, `[MarkNewPoly]`,
`[MarkNewPoly_Name]`, `[MarkNewCategory]`, `[PathToMarksIcons]` copied verbatim with
`awk` (section header through the line before the next header). CRLF line ends kept; the source file starts with a
UTF-8 BOM, the extract does not (its first section is not the first line of the source). Nothing edited by hand.
**Exercises**: marks system config, mark templates, name generators, category factory config read/write round trip
(docs/specs/marks.md sections 2.3 and 2.6).

## `system_nocase_vectors.tsv` (added 2026-10-12 with T-0062)

**Origin**: generated by `tools/gen_system_nocase_vectors.py` (formula-defined vectors, protocol rule 10). The script
is a statement-by-statement Python transcription of the Pascal source of the mORMot 2 library legacy links
(checkout `2.4.17538`, head `b770705`, 2026-10-11; the legacy tree pins no revision): `Utf8_SYSTEMNOCASE`
(`db/mormot.db.raw.sqlite3.pas:6328-6341`), `Utf8ILComp` (`core/mormot.core.unicode.pas:7683-7798`), `UTF8_TABLE`
(`:84-107`) and the `WinAnsiToUp` table (`:12572-12581`, copied verbatim). It shares no code with the C++ port
(`src/sas/marks/mormot/system_nocase.cpp`); two implementations of one source agreeing is the proof
available without a Windows run. Caveat: the Python generator is a second transcription of the same Pascal source by the
same author, so it catches slips, not a shared misreading of the source. Integer model: the 64-bit Windows build. An input for which the Pascal indexes its
table out of bounds makes the script raise, so no such vector exists (legacy-defects L-166).
**Format**: `<hex of a>` TAB `<hex of b>` TAB `<sign: -1|0|1>` TAB `<branch label>`; `-` is the empty string; `#` lines
are comments. 928 vectors: empty strings, the ASCII path (case, punctuation between `Z` and `a`, embedded NUL,
prefixes), every code point U+0080…U+00FF against its table image / `Z` / `ß`, the U+00FF/U+0100 boundary, Cyrillic
and Greek (case-sensitive), 3- and 4-byte sequences, 5- and 6-byte lead bytes, overlong and unvalidated continuation
bytes, invalid lead bytes and truncated sequences on either side, equal prefixes of different length.
**Regenerate**: `tools/gen_system_nocase_vectors.py` from the repository root (the test checks the vector count).
**Not yet proven** (needs the populated Windows file of docs/specs/marks.md §7.4, U-2): the same order observed in an
index page written by Windows SAS.Planet with more than one row.
